_note: CANONICAL DATA. This file is the campaign-finance FILING REGIME REGISTRY, read by
lib/control-plane/campaign-finance/filing-regime.ts and routed through by
lib/control-plane/campaign-finance/authority.ts. It is hand-maintained and is NOT a
generated artifact.
IT IS WHAT THIS PROJECT KNOWS NOW. It is NEVER a complete list of American campaign-finance
filing regimes, and it may never be read as one. There are fifty states, the District, the
territories, and tens of thousands of local filing jurisdictions below them; two jurisdictions
are recorded here. A jurisdiction that is ABSENT from this file resolves to the explicit
NO_REGIME_ON_RECORD routing state, which keeps the contest OPEN and names the statute-reading
route still owed. Absence from this file is a fact about this file. It is never a fact about a
government, and it never closes a contest.
EVERY REGIME HERE CARRIES PROVENANCE THIS REPOSITORY HAS ACTUALLY READ. A statutory quote is
the operative sentence verbatim, from the government's own site, with the URL and the date it
was read — never a paraphrase, because a paraphrase of a routing rule is a different routing
rule. Where a statute has NOT been read, statutoryBasis and statutoryQuote are null and
openQuestion says what is owed. A plausible citation typed from memory would be a fabrication
in the one field whose whole job is being checkable.
ADDING A JURISDICTION IS A DATA CHANGE. Add its row to `jurisdictions`, add one regime per
routing rule its statute states, and the domain code routes it with no edit under lib/. That
is asserted by tests/filing-regime-registry.test.ts against a clearly-marked fixture
jurisdiction, so the claim is checked rather than believed.

noRegimeRoutes.label: Read the jurisdiction's filing-officer statute from the legislature's own site
noRegimeRoutes.note: The generalising question, asked of every state: which statute defines the filing officer, and what does it route to whom? Answered for AZ (A.R.S. § 16-928), NH (RSA 664:7 and 664:6) and NJ. Unanswered for any jurisdiction absent from this registry. A jurisdiction we have not read is a jurisdiction we have not read — never a jurisdiction with no filing officer.
